note: What to look for in a small business contract, by kind. A plain checklist under Legal row 9 (C3): it names the topics and says where a lawyer should look; it never writes, changes or recommends legal terms. Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions run on the contract text.

parties.label: Who it is between
parties.why: Both legal names: yours (or your LLC's) and theirs, as they appear on official records.

scope.label: What is being done or delivered
scope.why: A clear list of the work or what is delivered, so both sides know what is included.
scope.look: \b(scope|services|deliverables?|statement of work|description of (the )?(work|services)|work to be performed)\b

price.label: Price
price.why: The amount, or the rate and how it adds up.

payment.label: When and how payment happens
payment.why: When payment is due, any deposit, and how to pay.

dates.label: Start, end and key dates
dates.why: When it starts, when it ends, and any deadlines.
dates.look: \b(effective (date|on|as of)|initial term|the term (is|of)|start date|commence\w*|end date|completion date|expir\w*|term of|deadline|schedule)\b

ending.label: How either side can end it
ending.why: How and when either side can end the agreement, and what happens then.

changes.label: How changes are handled
changes.why: How changes to the work or the terms get agreed.

liability.label: Limits on what either side could owe
liability.why: Whether there is a limit on what either side could owe if something goes wrong.
liability.look: limitation of liability|liabilit(y|ies)\s+(is|are|shall be|will be)\s+limited|in no event shall|shall not exceed|will not exceed|maximum liability

disputes.label: What happens in a disagreement
disputes.why: Which state's law applies and how disagreements are handled.

signatures.label: Signature lines with names, titles and dates
signatures.why: Signature lines with names, titles and dates for each side.

service.title: Work you do for a client
service.examples: A client agreement, service contract, statement of work or estimate they sign

items.label: Cancellations and rescheduling
items.why: How cancelling or rescheduling a visit works, and any charge for it.

items.label: What you stand behind after the job
items.why: Whether there is any promise about the work after it is done, and for how long.

items.label: Insurance
items.why: Whether any insurance is required, of what kind and how much.

items.label: Who owns what you make
items.why: Who owns what gets made, or who may use it.

items.label: Access, materials and permits
items.why: Who provides materials, site access and permits, and who pays for them.

contractor.title: Someone you hire as a contractor (1099)

items.label: They are an independent contractor
items.why: Whether it calls the worker an independent contractor. The label alone does not decide worker status: ask a pro.

items.label: Their insurance
items.why: Whether any insurance is required, of what kind and how much.

items.label: You own the work you pay for
items.why: Who owns what gets made, or who may use it.

items.label: Keeping your clients and info private
items.why: Whether either side must keep information private.

vendor.title: Something you buy or subscribe to
vendor.examples: Software, equipment, a supplier, marketing or a service you pay for

items.label: Renewal and price increases
items.why: Whether it renews, how to cancel, and whether the price can change.

items.label: Your data
items.why: What happens to your data, and whether you can export it.

items.label: What happens if it doesn't work
items.why: What they promise about uptime or delivery, and what happens if they miss it.

nda.title: A confidentiality agreement (NDA)
nda.examples: An NDA from a client, partner or contractor

items.label: What does not count
items.why: What is left out of confidential information.

items.label: How long it lasts
items.why: How long the duty to keep things private lasts.

items.label: Returning or deleting info
items.why: What happens to the information at the end.

risks.label: Renews on its own
risks.why: It renews unless someone cancels in time. Note the cancel-by date.

risks.label: Covering the other side's losses (indemnify)
risks.why: One side agrees to cover the other's losses or claims. Ask a lawyer what this means for you.

risks.label: Personal responsibility for payment
risks.why: You, not just your business, may be responsible for payment. Ask a lawyer before you sign.

risks.label: Limits on where or for whom you can work
risks.why: It limits where or for whom someone can work, or whom they can hire. Rules differ by state: ask a lawyer.

risks.label: Exclusive
risks.why: It may stop one side working with others. Ask a lawyer what it covers.

risks.label: They own everything you make
risks.why: It says who owns the work and anything made for the job. Ask a lawyer what it covers.
risks.look: work(s)? made for hire|work for hire|all (right,? title and interest|rights|intellectual property|work product)|assigns? (all|any and all)

risks.label: One side can change the terms
risks.why: One side can change the terms without the other agreeing. Ask a lawyer what this means for you.
risks.look: (reserves? the right|may|can) (to )?(modify|change|amend|update) (this|these|the) (agreement|terms)|at any time (and )?without (prior )?notice|in (its|our) sole discretion

risks.label: Fees or interest on late payment
risks.why: It sets fees or interest on late payment. Check the amounts and when they start.

risks.label: Arbitration or no jury
risks.why: Disagreements go to arbitration, or a jury trial is given up. Ask a lawyer what this means for you.

risks.label: You get paid only when they get paid
risks.why: Payment depends on someone else paying first. Note when you would actually be paid.

risks.label: Long notice to cancel
risks.why: Ending it takes 60 days' notice or more. Note the date you would need to give notice by.

risks.label: Slow payment terms
risks.why: Payment comes 45 days or more after the invoice. Plan for the wait.

risks.label: Confession of judgment
risks.why: This kind of clause can have serious effects. Ask a lawyer before you sign.

risks.label: As is, no promises
risks.why: It says there is no promise about how well it works. Ask what support they offer.

disclaimer: This is a checklist, not legal advice, and it can miss things or flag wording that is fine. It does not say whether anything is legal, enforceable or right for you. Before you sign anything, have a lawyer licensed in your state read it. Many state and local bar associations run lawyer referral services.
